I live in Langley and help buyers find condos with an age-restriction bylaw, from downtown Langley City to Murrayville and the riverfront at Fort Langley. I've been a REALTOR® since 2015 and a member of the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board's Medallion Club for 10 straight years, which puts me in the top 1% of all Realtors in the Fraser Valley by FVREB sales. I've also closed more than $500M in sales.

Below are condos for sale in Langley City and the Township of Langley whose MLS® listings are marked with an age-restriction bylaw. Read the strata bylaws and Form B on each one to confirm the exact rule.

For many Langley buyers, a condo means walking to coffee, groceries and appointments instead of driving. Condos here are spread between the City of Langley around the downtown core and parts of the Township, including Murrayville, Willoughby, Walnut Grove and the riverfront at Fort Langley.

Condo listings marked with an age-restriction bylaw have included homes in buildings such as Wheatcroft Manor, Parkway, Residences at Village Square and Waterfront at Bedford Landing. That doesn't mean any of those buildings has an age bylaw today. Owners can vote to add, change or remove bylaws, so the list below uses each listing's bylaw flag rather than a building name.
There are usually fewer of these condos on the market than townhomes, so it helps to set up an alert and move quickly when the right one comes up.

Downtown Langley City is the most walkable choice. Apartment buildings sit close to the Fraser Highway One-Way, with shops, clinics and bus routes nearby, and the Nicomekl River trails a short walk south. For more on the City, see my
City of Langley condos for sale
page.

Murrayville sits on both sides of Fraser Highway, just east of the City, and has a smaller village centre with Langley Memorial Hospital close by. Fort Langley is a small village on the Fraser River, with a handful of condo buildings near Glover Road and the riverfront. Willoughby and Walnut Grove have newer apartment buildings near larger shopping centres. Each area has its own community plan, which you can explore in my
Langley neighbourhood guides

blocks.text: What the age bylaw means here

parts.t: In BC, a strata corporation can pass a bylaw requiring one or more people living in a strata lot to be at least a set age, and it can't set that age below 55 (
Strata Property Act, section 123.1

). Section 123.2 covers exceptions, such as someone who lived in the unit before the bylaw passed, and some caregivers. Owners can vote to change a bylaw, so always read the current registered version.

The MLS® flag is entered by the listing agent. It doesn't show the exact age, whether it applies to one resident or all of them, or how the strata enforces it. I can request the bylaws and Form B for any condo on this page before you make an offer.

blocks.text: What to check in a Langley condo building

parts.t: The exact bylaw.
Read the registered bylaws for the age, who it covers, and rules on guests or caregivers.
Fees and levies.
The Form B shows the monthly fee, approved special levies and the contingency reserve fund.
Building systems.
The depreciation report covers elevators, roofs, windows and piping. Ask what work has been done and what's planned.
Flood and river areas.
Some downtown and Fort Langley buildings sit near the Nicomekl or Fraser River, so ask about insurance and the strata's deductible.
Everyday access.
Elevator access, steps at the entry, and how far the parking stall and storage locker are from the unit.

What is a 55+ condo in Langley?

On this page it means a condo in Langley City or the Township whose MLS® listing is marked with an age-restriction bylaw. BC stratas can require one or more residents to be at least a set age, not lower than 55.
Are the buildings named on this page age-restricted?

Not necessarily. Listings have included homes in Wheatcroft Manor, Parkway, Residences at Village Square and Waterfront at Bedford Landing, but this page does not claim any building is age-restricted. Bylaws can change by vote.
How do I confirm a building's age bylaw?
Ask for the registered strata bylaws and the Form B Information Certificate, and read recent minutes. I can request these for any listing before you write an offer.
Can a younger spouse or partner live with me?
It depends on the wording. Some bylaws require only one resident to meet the age, and others require every resident. Read the registered bylaws before you buy.
Which part of Langley is most walkable for a condo?
Downtown Langley City is usually the most walkable, with shops, clinics and transit close by. Murrayville and Fort Langley have smaller village centres.
Can you help me sell my house and buy a 55+ condo?
Yes. Most buyers on this page are also selling. Start with a free home evaluation, then call or text me at 604-928-1361 to plan the timing of both moves.
Why does the list change so often?
The listings come from MLS® and update daily. Units sell, new ones are listed, and the age flag is entered by each listing agent, so use the live list rather than a building name alone.
